claim: Bacterial efflux pumps confer multidrug resistance by transporting diverse antibiotics from the cell.
source: Bacterial efflux pumps confer multidrug resistance by transporting diverse antibiotics from the cell.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about bacterial efflux pumps and their role in antibiotic resistance.

claim: In Gram-negative bacteria, some efflux pumps form multi-protein assemblies that span the cell envelope.
source: In Gram-negative bacteria, some of these pumps form multi-protein assemblies that span the cell envelope.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and citations in the manuscript.

claim: Near-atomic resolution cryoEM structures of the Escherichia coli AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump in resting and drug transport states have been determined.
source: Here, we report the near-atomic resolution cryoEM structures of the Escherichia coli AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump in resting and drug transport states, revealing a quaternary structural switch that allosterically couples and synchronizes initial ligand binding with channel opening.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the study, supported by the cryoEM data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: A quaternary structural switch allosterically couples and synchronizes initial ligand binding with channel opening in the AcrAB-TolC pump.
source: Here, we report the near-atomic resolution cryoEM structures of the Escherichia coli AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump in resting and drug transport states, revealing a quaternary structural switch that allosterically couples and synchronizes initial ligand binding with channel opening.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural data obtained in the study.

claim: Within the transport-activated state, the channel remains open even though the pump cycles through three distinct conformations.
source: Within the transport-activated state, the channel remains open even though the pump cycles through three distinct conformations.
evidence: This is based on structural observations from the cryoEM data.

claim: Drug efflux pumps play important roles in intrinsic or acquired drug resistance to a wide variety of currently available antimicrobial agents.
source: Drug efflux pumps play important roles in intrinsic or acquired drug resistance to a wide variety of currently available antimicrobial agents (Pu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The components of tripartite efflux assemblies include an outer membrane protein, a plasma membrane-spanning protein and a periplasmic protein that connects the two trans-membrane components.
source: The components of these assemblies include an outer membrane protein, a plasma membrane-spanning protein and a periplasmic protein that connects the two trans-membrane components (Du et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: AcrAB-TolC is a RND-based tripartite efflux pump comprised of TolC, AcrA, and AcrB.
source: AcrAB-TolC is a RND-based tripartite efflux pump, comprised of the outer membrane protein TolC, the periplasmic membrane fusion protein AcrA, and the inner membrane transporter AcrB, which cycles through three different conformational states during the drug transport process: access (L), binding (T) and extrusion (O) (Du et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: AcrB cycles through three different conformational states during the drug transport process: access (L), binding (T) and extrusion (O).
source: AcrAB-TolC is a RND-based tripartite efflux pump, comprised of the outer membrane protein TolC, the periplasmic membrane fusion protein AcrA, and the inner membrane transporter AcrB, which cycles through three different conformational states during the drug transport process: access (L), binding (T) and extrusion (O) (Du et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: AcrZ is a small peptide that modifies the activity of AcrB.
source: A small peptide, AcrZ, has been identified that modifies the activity of AcrB (Hobbs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Previous electron microscopy studies of the AcrAB-TolC pump have revealed the overall shape of the pump and the relative arrangement of its components.
source: Previous electron microscopy studies of the AcrAB-TolC pump have revealed the overall shape of the pump and the relative arrangement of its components (Daury et al., 2016; Du et al., 2014; Jeong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Previous electron microscopy studies were unable to identify the detailed interaction interfaces between the components due to limited resolution.
source: Due to the limited resolution, these studies were unable to identify the detailed interaction interfaces between the components.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of prior studies cited.

claim: The mechanism of pump assembly and channel opening is presently unclear.
source: Moreover, the mechanism of pump assembly and channel opening is presently unclear (Müller and Pos, 2015; Zgurskaya et al., 2015) and requires detailed structural information of the pump in the different conformational states that accompany drug translocation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature indicating gaps in knowledge.

claim: The quality of the cryoEM maps enable unambiguous modeling of all components and identification of the conformational asymmetry in AcrB in the presence of antibiotic.
source: The quality of the cryoEM maps enable unambiguous modeling of all components and identification of the conformational asymmetry in AcrB in the presence of antibiotic that underpins the molecular mechanism of drug translocation.
evidence: This is based on the experimental data obtained in the study.

claim: The fusion construct was co-expressed with AcrZ, a hydrophobic helical peptide that affects AcrB efflux activity for a subset of antibiotics.
source: The fusion was co-expressed with AcrZ, a hydrophobic helical peptide that affects AcrB efflux activity for a subset of antibiotics (Hobbs et al., 2012) and interacts with AcrB in the transmembrane portion (Du et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: AcrZ interacts with AcrB in the transmembrane portion.
source: The fusion was co-expressed with AcrZ, a hydrophobic helical peptide that affects AcrB efflux activity for a subset of antibiotics (Hobbs et al., 2012) and interacts with AcrB in the transmembrane portion (Du et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The ratio of detergent to total membrane protein was optimized to extract AcrAB-TolC from the cellular membrane.
source: The ratio of detergent to total membrane protein was optimized to extract AcrAB-TolC from the cellular membrane, and the detergent was exchanged with amphipol A8-35 (Baker et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2013; Popot, 2010; Tribet et al., 1996; Zoonens and Popot, 2014).
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the experimental procedures.

claim: The detergent was exchanged with amphipol A8-35.
source: The ratio of detergent to total membrane protein was optimized to extract AcrAB-TolC from the cellular membrane, and the detergent was exchanged with amphipol A8-35 (Baker et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2013; Popot, 2010; Tribet et al., 1996; Zoonens and Popot, 2014).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citations to prior literature on amphipol use.

claim: Ligands were used in an effort to favor conformational uniformity and/or to capture structures corresponding to different ligand transport states.
source: Ligands were used in an effort to favor conformational uniformity and/or to capture structures corresponding to different ligand transport states.
evidence: This is a methodological rationale from the experimental design.

claim: The purified pump was imaged in the presence of pyranopyridine inhibitor MBX3132.
source: The purified pump was imaged in the presence of pyranopyridine inhibitor MBX3132 (Sjuts et al., 2016) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B; Supplementary file 1) or substrate puromycin, as described in Materials and methods.
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the manuscript and shown in figures.

claim: The purified pump was imaged in the presence of substrate puromycin.
source: The purified pump was imaged in the presence of pyranopyridine inhibitor MBX3132 (Sjuts et al., 2016) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B; Supplementary file 1) or substrate puromycin, as described in Materials and methods.
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the manuscript.

claim: A new procedure was developed to stabilize the full pump using disulphide-linkages between residues S273 in AcrA and S258 in AcrB.
source: We also have developed a new procedure to stabilize the full pump using disulphide-linkages that were chosen from the proximity of residues S273 in the β-barrel domain of AcrA and S258 in the β-hairpin motif of the DN subdomain of AcrB seen in the cryo-EM structure of the full pump.
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the manuscript.

claim: Disulfide bond formation was observed between AcrA-S273C and AcrB-S258C components.
source: We introduced single cysteine-substitutions in the individual AcrA and AcrB components (AcrA-S273C and AcrB-S258C) without flexible engineered linkers. Consistent with the model based on the fusion constructs, we observed disulfide bond formation between the two free components.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: The disulfide bond-stabilized AcrAB can recruit TolC to form a stable tripartite complex in vivo.
source: Moreover, the disulfide bond-stabilized AcrAB can recruit TolC (and three additional AcrAs, which are not expected to be cysteine-crosslinked) to form a stable tripartite complex in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in the figure.

claim: The cryo-EM structures of the apo pump and the pump/ligand complexes reveal different conformational states of the full pump.
source: The cryo-EM structures of the apo pump and the pump/ligand complexes reveal different conformational states of the full pump.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural findings from the study.

claim: The structures have been solved at different subnanometer and near atomic resolutions.
source: These structures have been solved at different subnanometer and near atomic resolutions (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a statement about the resolution of the structures obtained.

claim: The maps of the full pump at 3.6 Å resolution can be readily segmented into a TolC trimer, a periplasmic AcrA hexamer, and an AcrB trimer.
source: The maps of the full pump at 3.6 Å resolution can be readily segmented into a TolC trimer, a periplasmic AcrA hexamer, and an AcrB trimer (Video 1).
evidence: This is a description of the structural composition observed in the cryoEM maps.

claim: The reconstruction of the apo pump was achieved at 6.5 Å resolution.
source: The reconstruction of the apo pump at 6.5 Å resolution (Supplementary file 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 4) revealed TolC to be in the closed conformational state (Figure 1), like that seen in the crystal structure of the isolated protein (Koronakis et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement about the resolution achieved for the apo pump structure.

claim: TolC in the apo pump is in the closed conformational state.
source: The reconstruction of the apo pump at 6.5 Å resolution (Supplementary file 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 4) revealed TolC to be in the closed conformational state (Figure 1), like that seen in the crystal structure of the isolated protein (Koronakis et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data, supported by comparison to crystal structure.

claim: The periplasmic component AcrA forms a hexamer through the trimerization of two conformationally distinct protomers.
source: The periplasmic component of the pump, AcrA, forms a hexamer through the trimerization of two conformationally distinct protomers (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: In both AcrA protomers, a short helix-turn-helix (HTH) motif interacts in a tip-to-tip manner with the HTH motif of the TolC coiled-coils at their periplasmic ends.
source: In both AcrA protomers, a short helix-turn-helix (HTH) motif interacts in a tip-to-tip manner with the HTH motif of the TolC coiled-coils at their periplasmic ends (Figure 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: Each subunit of TolC has an internal structural repeat.
source: Because each subunit of TolC has an internal structural repeat, the trimer has 6 HTH motifs, which interact with the 6 HTH motifs of the AcrA hexamer in a quasi-equivalent manner: AcrA protomer-I and the adjacent protomer-II interdigitate with the intra- and inter-protomer grooves of TolC, respectively.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge of TolC.

claim: The TolC trimer has 6 HTH motifs, which interact with the 6 HTH motifs of the AcrA hexamer in a quasi-equivalent manner.
source: Because each subunit of TolC has an internal structural repeat, the trimer has 6 HTH motifs, which interact with the 6 HTH motifs of the AcrA hexamer in a quasi-equivalent manner: AcrA protomer-I and the adjacent protomer-II interdigitate with the intra- and inter-protomer grooves of TolC, respectively.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: AcrA protomer-I and the adjacent protomer-II interdigitate with the intra- and inter-protomer grooves of TolC, respectively.
source: Because each subunit of TolC has an internal structural repeat, the trimer has 6 HTH motifs, which interact with the 6 HTH motifs of the AcrA hexamer in a quasi-equivalent manner: AcrA protomer-I and the adjacent protomer-II interdigitate with the intra- and inter-protomer grooves of TolC, respectively.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The two distinct conformations of the HTH motif loops of AcrA protomers I and II structurally conform to the slightly different contact surfaces of TolC.
source: The two distinct conformations of the HTH motif loops of AcrA protomers I and II structurally conform to the slightly different contact surfaces of TolC (Figure 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: This interaction is consistent with functional and structural data.
source: This interaction is consistent with functional (Lee et al., 2012; Song et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2010) and structural data (Daury et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2015), but differs in detail from that proposed for the open state of the pump reported earlier (Jeong et al., 2016), as we will describe further below.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior functional and structural studies.

claim: A gap is present at the interfaces between adjacent AcrA dimer pairs in the apo state.
source: A gap is present at the interfaces between adjacent AcrA dimer pairs, so that the AcrA helical hairpin, lipoyl and β-barrel domains do not pack tightly to seal the channel from the periplasm (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The AcrA helical hairpin, lipoyl and β-barrel domains do not pack tightly to seal the channel from the periplasm in the apo state.
source: A gap is present at the interfaces between adjacent AcrA dimer pairs, so that the AcrA helical hairpin, lipoyl and β-barrel domains do not pack tightly to seal the channel from the periplasm (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: This gap must be closed in the transport process to prevent leakage of substrates into the periplasm.
source: This gap must be closed in the transport process to prevent leakage of substrates into the periplasm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation and functional requirements.

claim: AcrB adopts a symmetric state (LLL) in the apo pump assembly.
source: AcrB adopts a symmetric state (LLL) in the pump assembly, as seen in the crystal structure of apo AcrB (Murakami et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by comparison to crystal structure.

claim: Crystallographic studies of AcrB in complex with natural substrates reveal asymmetric structures, which suggest consecutive steps of a transport cycle.
source: The crystallographic studies of AcrB in complex with natural substrates reveal asymmetric structures, which suggest consecutive steps of a transport cycle (Murakami et al., 2006; Seeger et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior crystallographic studies.

claim: Puromycin is a validated transport substrate for AcrB.
source: We explored how the full pump accommodates AcrB in this functional state in the presence of puromycin, which is a validated transport substrate (Hobbs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A focused classification procedure identified a subset of the full pump assembly (30.2% of the entire dataset) containing exactly one protomer in the extrusion state (O) of AcrB.
source: We targeted the AcrB protomers using a focused classification procedure (Bai et al., 2015) (See Materials and methods) and could identify a subset of the full pump assembly (30.2% of the entire dataset) containing exactly one protomer whose density matches the extrusion state (O) of AcrB, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis of the cryoEM data.

claim: A 5.9 Å density map of the full pump assembly without any imposed symmetry was reconstructed from the particle subset containing the O state.
source: A 5.9 Å density map of the full pump assembly without any imposed symmetry was reconstructed from this particle subset (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the cryoEM reconstruction.

claim: The three AcrB protomers in L, O and T states are in a fixed spatial relationship with respect to each other in the full pump assembly.
source: The correlation analysis of the map region corresponding to the AcrBZ components shows that the three AcrB protomers in L, O and T states are in a fixed spatial relationship with respect to each other in this full pump assembly (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis of the cryoEM map.

claim: The spatial disposition of AcrB protomers fits very well to the crystal structures of numerous other drug-bound AcrB structures.
source: This spatial disposition fits very well to the crystal structures of numerous other drug-bound AcrB structures (Eicher et al., 2012; Murakami et al., 2006; Nakashima et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior crystal structures cited.

claim: No puromycin density is detected in the cryoEM map of the pump in the presence of puromycin.
source: Though the AcrB subunit densities match well with those in the crystal structure, no puromycin density is detected in the cryoEM map.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryoEM map.

claim: A similar situation occurs for some crystal structures of the asymmetric state, where drug is present in the buffer but discernable electron density for the drug is absent from the ligand binding pockets.
source: A similar situation occurs for some crystal structures of the asymmetric state, where drug is present in the buffer but discernable electron density for the drug is absent from the ligand binding pockets (Seeger et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior crystallographic studies.

claim: The crystal structure of AcrBZ in the presence of puromycin was determined at 3.2 Å resolution.
source: The crystal structure of AcrBZ in the presence of puromycin at 3.2 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Supplementary file 3) shows that the AcrB subunits adopt three distinct conformational states (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) as seen in our cryoEM structure in the presence of this drug.
evidence: This is a result from X-ray crystallography.

claim: The AcrB subunits adopt three distinct conformational states in the crystal structure with puromycin.
source: The crystal structure of AcrBZ in the presence of puromycin at 3.2 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Supplementary file 3) shows that the AcrB subunits adopt three distinct conformational states (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) as seen in our cryoEM structure in the presence of this drug.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Poorly defined density for puromycin is found in the binding pocket of the T protomer in the crystal structure.
source: Poorly defined density for puromycin is found in the binding pocket of the T protomer (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is an observation from the crystal structure electron density map.

claim: TolC adopts a fully opened state via tip-to-tip interactions with AcrA in the pump assembly with puromycin.
source: TolC adopts a fully opened state via tip-to-tip interactions with AcrA in the pump assembly and AcrAs pack tightly to form a sealed channel, which is similar to that seen in the complex of the pump with the potent inhibitor MBX3132, to which we now turn.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: AcrAs pack tightly to form a sealed channel in the pump assembly with puromycin.
source: TolC adopts a fully opened state via tip-to-tip interactions with AcrA in the pump assembly and AcrAs pack tightly to form a sealed channel, which is similar to that seen in the complex of the pump with the potent inhibitor MBX3132, to which we now turn.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: MBX3132 likely binds AcrB tightly, since it is active in the nanomolar concentration range.
source: The inhibitor MBX3132 likely binds AcrB tightly, since it is active in the nanomolar concentration range (Sjuts et al., 2016), and the compound was used to lock the pump in a more homogeneous conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known activity of the inhibitor cited.

claim: The 3D map for the pump/MBX3132 complex was initially generated without any imposed symmetry and exhibited an apparent 3-fold symmetric pattern.
source: The 3D map for the pump/MBX3132 complex was initially generated without any imposed symmetry and exhibited an apparent 3-fold symmetric pattern (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from the initial cryoEM reconstruction.

claim: Refinements with 3-fold symmetry produced the final 3D reconstruction at ~3.6 Å resolution for the pump/MBX3132 complex.
source: Thus, refinements were performed with 3-fold symmetry, which produced the final 3D reconstruction at ~3.6 Å resolution.
evidence: This is a result from the cryoEM reconstruction process.

claim: 73% of the particles within the MBX3132 dataset have their three AcrB subunits in the same (TTT) conformation.
source: We found that 73% of the particles within the dataset have their three AcrB subunits in the same (TTT) conformation (Materials and method and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: This is a result from the focused 3D classification analysis.

claim: Subsets of particles show AcrB conformations in LLL (1.4%), LLT (6.2%) and LTT (18.6%) states in the MBX3132 dataset.
source: Subsets of particles show AcrB conformations in LLL (1.4%), LLT (6.2%) and LTT (18.6%) states, respectively, while none of the subunits was identified in an 'O' state.
evidence: This is a result from the focused 3D classification analysis.

claim: None of the AcrB subunits was identified in an 'O' state in the MBX3132 dataset.
source: Subsets of particles show AcrB conformations in LLL (1.4%), LLT (6.2%) and LTT (18.6%) states, respectively, while none of the subunits was identified in an 'O' state.
evidence: This is a result from the focused 3D classification analysis.

claim: The inhibitor-bound pump conformation primarily represents a T-saturated state of the AcrB.
source: Therefore, this inhibitor-bound pump conformation primarily represents a T-saturated state of the AcrB.
evidence: This is an inference based on the classification results showing predominance of TTT state.

claim: The C3 symmetry imposed reconstruction using the subset of particles with TTT state achieved 3.6 Å resolution.
source: The C3 symmetry imposed reconstruction using the subset of particles with TTT state (24,597 particles) also achieved 3.6 Å resolution (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is a result from the cryoEM reconstruction.

claim: Clear density for the inhibitor MBX3132 was observed in a 'hydrophobic trap' site adjacent to the drug binding of the AcrB trimer.
source: We observed clear density for the inhibitor in a 'hydrophobic trap' site adjacent to the drug binding of the AcrB trimer in both the asymmetric and symmetry imposed maps (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryoEM density maps.

claim: Side chains can be readily assigned and modeled in the protruding densities along the peptide backbone in the 3.6 Å structure.
source: Side chains can be readily assigned and modeled in the protruding densities along the peptide backbone (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the cryoEM map.

claim: TolC adopts a fully opened state through an iris-like dilation of the periplasmic end.
source: Comparing the structure of TolC in the crystal or in the apo pump with that in the inhibitor-bound pump assembly reveals that TolC adopts a fully opened state through an iris-like dilation of the periplasmic end.
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing different states.

claim: The iris-like dilation is presumably necessary to maintain TolC-AcrA connectivity and to permit drug molecules to pass through the pump.
source: This dilation is presumably necessary to maintain TolC-AcrA connectivity and to permit drug molecules to pass through the pump (Koronakis et al., 2000).
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the structural change, supported by citation.

claim: Little conformational change is shown in the TolC TM region and the adjacent α-helical portion.
source: Little conformational change is shown in the TolC TM region and the adjacent α-helical portion.
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing different states.

claim: The structures start to deviate at the equatorial domain, where the superhelical trajectories of coiled-coil helices change with the iris-like dilation.
source: However, the structures start to deviate at the equatorial domain, where the superhelical trajectories of coiled-coil helices change with the iris-like dilation (Figure 4A and B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing different states.

claim: In the 'closed state' conformation, the constriction is maintained by an inter-protomer hydrogen-bonding network, involving R367 in one subunit and T152, D153 and Y362 in the adjacent subunit.
source: In the 'closed state' conformation, seen in the apo pump, the constriction is maintained by an inter-protomer hydrogen-bonding network, involving R367 in one subunit and T152, D153 and Y362 in the adjacent subunit (Andersen et al., 2002; Augustus et al., 2004; Bavro et al., 2008)(Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The hydrogen-bonding network is broken in the TolC of pump/MBX3132 complex.
source: This network of interactions is broken in the TolC of pump/MBX3132 complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) and the pump/puromycin complex.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM structures.

claim: The hydrogen-bonding network is broken in the TolC of pump/puromycin complex.
source: This network of interactions is broken in the TolC of pump/MBX3132 complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) and the pump/puromycin complex.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM structures.

claim: Tip-to-tip interactions of the AcrA and TolC HTH motifs are observed in the ligand-bound pump structures.
source: We observe tip-to-tip interactions of the AcrA and TolC HTH motifs (Figure 4), which is similar to that proposed for the open state of the pump reported earlier (Jeong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data, consistent with prior proposals.

claim: These interactions account for the importance of the conserved Val-Gly-Leu/Thr element of TolC.
source: These interactions account for the importance of the conserved Val-Gly-Leu/Thr element of TolC (Jeong et al., 2016; Song et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference about functional significance supported by citations.

claim: At the AcrA protomer-I/TolC interface, contacts involve the backbone of G365 in the conserved VGL motif of TolC with the backbone of K140 and side chain of S139 in AcrA.
source: At the AcrA protomer-I/TolC interface, contacts involve the backbone of G365 in the conserved VGL motif of TolC with the backbone of K140 and side chain of S139 in AcrA (Jeong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data, consistent with prior work.

claim: N145 and T366 of TolC directly contact AcrA L132 in the pump.
source: The N145 and T366 of TolC directly contact AcrA L132 in the pump, consistent with the results of in vivo site-specific cross-linking experiments (Xu et al., 2011) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a structural observation consistent with prior cross-linking experiments.

claim: The cryoEM structure shows the presence of residue pairs at the interface between AcrA and TolC that were predicted to have co-evolved in homologous proteins in the MdtNOP efflux pump.
source: Our cryoEM structure shows the presence of residue pairs at the interface between AcrA and TolC (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) that were predicted to have co-evolved in the homologous proteins in a different efflux pump MdtNOP (Harley and Saier, 2000; Ovchinnikov et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a structural observation that validates prior co-evolution predictions.

claim: 3D classification identified a small subset of particles, in which TolC rotates by 60 degrees with respect to AcrA, but the alternative interface still retains the key contacts.
source: 3D classification identified a small subset of particles, in which TolC rotates by 60 degrees with respect to AcrA, but the alternative interface still retains the key contacts described above.
evidence: This is a result from the 3D classification analysis.

claim: There are two distinct conformations of the HTH motif loops of AcrA protomers I and II that structurally conform to the slightly different contact surfaces of TolC.
source: As observed in the apo state, there are two distinct conformations of the HTH motif loops of AcrA protomers I and II that structurally conform to the slightly different contact surfaces of TolC (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The flexibility of the HTH is consistent with observations from crystal structures.
source: The flexibility of the HTH is consistent with observations from crystal structures (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) (Mikolosko et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by comparison to crystal structures cited.

claim: In the six protomers of AcrA, the lipoyl and β-barrel domains form a stack of two continuous rings.
source: In the six protomers of AcrA, the lipoyl and β-barrel domains form a stack of two continuous rings.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The lipoyl domains have no interaction with either AcrB or TolC.
source: The lipoyl domains have no interaction with either AcrB or TolC, and the β-barrel domains contact only the docking domain of AcrB (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The β-barrel domains contact only the docking domain of AcrB.
source: The lipoyl domains have no interaction with either AcrB or TolC, and the β-barrel domains contact only the docking domain of AcrB (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The membrane-proximal (MP) domain of AcrA interacts with both the docking domain and the top of the pore domain of AcrB.
source: The membrane-proximal (MP) domain of AcrA interacts with both the docking domain and the top of the pore domain of AcrB.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: Each AcrB protomer makes two non-equivalent interactions with AcrA.
source: Each AcrB protomer makes two non-equivalent interactions with AcrA (Ntreh et al., 2016); i.e. each pair of AcrA protomers makes two conformationally distinct interfaces with AcrB, as was found with the interaction between AcrA and TolC (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by citation.

claim: AcrA protomer-I makes extensive interactions with AcrB.
source: AcrA protomer-I makes extensive interactions with AcrB.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The β-barrel domain of AcrA protomer-I docks on the DN and DC subdomains of AcrB.
source: The β-barrel domain of AcrA protomer-I docks on the DN and DC subdomains of AcrB, while its MP domain interacts with the PC1 subdomain, the linker region between PC2 and DC, and an extended loop of the DN subdomain from an adjacent AcrB protomer (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The pump is a highly allosteric system in which conformational changes associated with ligand binding by the apo state of AcrB are communicated over a long distance to TolC through the repacking of protein-protein interfaces.

claim: The apo-form of the pump with a closed TolC represents a resting state.
source: In this study, we have captured structures of the full pump assembly with a closed channel in the apo-state and with an opened channel in the presence of inhibitor or antibiotic. We propose that the apo-form of the pump with a closed TolC represents a resting state (Figure 1), while the pump assemblies with opened TolC in the presence of transportable ligands represent transport states, in which the AcrB trimer adopts asymmetric LLT, LTT or LTO conformations.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural data.
